language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.
language.lessonRating: How do you feel about this exercise?

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.

Hello! I'm Ike and I fish in the Arctic waters here in Iceland. Let me tell you, these frozen waters are no picnic! It's a wonder there's anything surviving
out there!
It can get down to -40 degree Celsius here in the winter! That's probably a little chillier than you are used to, huh?
When you are cold you probably put on a coat or a sweater, and maybe a hat and gloves. Maybe you drink some hot tea. That's your way of adapting to your surroundings.

Plants and animals have ways they adapt to the places they live in too. Ever noticed that a polar bear looks different from a grizzly bear? And did you ever wonder why a cactus might grow in the desert but not in the arctic?

Plants and animals have certain characteristics that help them survive in their environment. These are called adaptations. These adaptations help them control body temperature, find food, protect themselves, and improve movement.

out there!
It can get down to -40 degree Celsius here in the winter! That's probably a little chillier than you are used to, huh?
When you are cold you probably put on a coat or a sweater, and maybe a hat and gloves. Maybe you drink some hot tea. That's your way of adapting to your surroundings.

Plants and animals have ways they adapt to the places they live in too. Ever noticed that a polar bear looks different from a grizzly bear? And did you ever wonder why a cactus might grow in the desert but not in the arctic?

Plants and animals have certain characteristics that help them survive in their environment. These are called adaptations. These adaptations help them control body temperature, find food, protect themselves, and improve movement.

I am amazed by the fact that all these animals don't freeze to death! How are they able to do that? What adaptations help them survive? What do you think? Can you help me find out by selecting the traits that help the Arctic animals adapt to the environment?

Thanks for your help! Now I know the different behaviours and physical characteristics that help plants and animals to survive!

I can't, for the life of me, figure out whether the plants' and animals' adaptations are behavioural or structural. You see, there's a difference between the two. A behavioural adaptation means the things a plant or animal does to survive, like eating
or sleeping.
A structural adaptation means the things a plant or animal is or has to survive, like being really small or having thick fur. Alright, can you help me sort everything out?
